title: Grateful Dead Live at Soldiers and Sailors Memorial Hall on 1972-11-13
lineage: master #1: AUD MR>C>D>CD recorded by Bear(//Playing through Casey Jones// is all that circulates from this source)master #2: low generation AUD(supplies the rest of the show)

ai_review.summary: Rough audience tape but the show shines with an iconic Dark Star > Dew and high‑energy playing.
ai_review.review: The performance is celebrated for its monster Dark Star > Dew stretch, with Phil’s thunderous bass and Jerry’s wailing guitar driving a powerful mid‑show jam. Recording quality varies – Bear’s audience (AUD) segment sounds surprisingly clear while the rest of the set is muddy and occasionally choppy, making it a challenging listen that rewards patience.

ai_rating.rationale: Most reviewers rate the music highly (4‑5 stars) praising Dark Star > Dew and overall energy, while recording quality receives mixed comments; weighting yields a solid 4‑star overall rating.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Bear’s AUD portion is clear and well‑balanced; the remainder of the tape is muddy, with occasional dropouts and uneven mic placement that make early songs harder to follow.

show_quality.setlist_flow: The set revolves around a long Dark Star/Dew sequence that serves as the high‑point; other parts are solid but less remarkable, creating a flow that builds to an intense jam climax.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Jerry is described as wailing and delivering strong guitar work throughout the show.
band_member_comments.Phil: Phil’s bass 'thunders' and provides powerful moments, especially during the Dark Star/Dew stretch.
